ratings.reason: The diff does not change schedule resolution or the shared-schedule location, so it does not alter this entry's already-superseded status.
run.py keeps OBS = HERE / "observe", and export.py still emits records with "side": "model".

compile.py now sets Lifetime from the schedule as L in ticks, and Lease.tla adds clock offsets, early timers and ClockStep. Time and lifetime are no longer just the fixed abstract Lifetime = 1 reported on grants.
Pause and Resume retain their previous behavior, with no run-time or L-based resume guard added; C1.4's premise still excludes paused clients.
Elect now permits ~HearsLeader(n) \/ early[n], so after a forward clock step a node may stand for election even while hearing a current leader.
DoRequest still requires ~pending[c], leaving the T3 waiting behavior unchanged.
Issuance-time Grant recording and same-token Resend remain, while grants now carry config_epoch, counted eligible agreements and C3.5 inputs for changing configurations.
lastEv is now a sequence and Match1 handles v3 commit, refusal and agreement events, while Emit and ScheduleStep preserve arming and synchronous predecessor-event matching.
Quiescent now additionally covers reconfiguration messages, NoPending and operator outcomes, extending end-of-run quiescence to v3 without changing the existing schedule-step behavior.
Resolve adds trigger-time non-member resolution and Procs now includes operators, while grantor/holder still resolve through trigG and rest through the partition sides.
StaleTok and its use by DoWrite and DoRead are unchanged.
compile.py now accepts 1–6 lease nodes, one or more clients, config/operators and the F3 cells. The old exact 3/2/1 topology and previous cell-set restrictions no longer hold.
The X2 send-time link-fate semantics remain, while rcMsgs and associated crash/operator handling add v3 reconfiguration traffic to the message model.
Ordinary Crash/Restart retain durable storage state and lease-node promised/maxTok, while AmnesicRestart adds the separate F3.3 case with a new incarnation and no durable state.
C1_2 remains a history check over storage decisions; the added stored-value and input recording supports C3_5 without moving that check onto the ledger variable.
RecvAck and the exporter still identify writes by client, token and value, and an accepted WriteAck still represents being told success.
Good(c) retains the up/unpaused and direct-Conn requirements but now uses eligible majorities of GLatest and NoPending; C1_4 still uses <>[]Good(c).
C1_4 still expresses completion as pending[c] becoming false, and a client crash still clears that wait.
The PASS witness and its trace-export role are retained; the added reach and replay checks do not change the witness policy described here.
export.py now identifies records by (proc, inc, seq), starts seq at zero and resets it per incarnation, rather than maintaining the old single per-process sequence.
P3 still breaks the token increment and P7 still acknowledges before a volatile storage decision; their surrounding X3 frames changed, not these placements.
ScheduleStep still offers lastEv' synchronously, but lastEv' is now a sequence and v3 events are matched, extending the same T1 behavior to X3 steps.
The existing client and storage in-flight clauses remain, and Quiescent adds reconfiguration requests, pending requests and operator outcomes for v3.
Resolved still leaves an unresolvable alias waiting, while Resolve, NMChoices and trigNM add trigger-time resolution of the new non-member selector.
static_checks retains conservative maybe_down/maybe_paused alias tracking and now applies its restart reasoning to aliased amnesic restarts and the new v5 actions.
Join still raises lagging promises over the leader-to-node link, now as a heartbeat scoped to the current configuration and a requested next membership.
trigNG is still computed from up' and LastGrant' when the trigger fires, preserving the post-event or post-action evaluation timing.
NGChoices still uses trigNG, or ngDown for the special restart case, so an empty candidate set still leaves ScheduleStep without a resolution.
DoRead still assigns rid |-> pc, and the exporter continues to key read attempts and decisions by client and read id.
The C2_1 history-based check and rdecisions history are retained; the new recorded-input fields do not move the check onto storage's ledger variable.
StorageRead still leaves highest unchanged on both served and rejected decisions, preserving the ha = hb check.
StorageRead still uses stval at the decision and records held separately; the adaptation only adds exported stored-value and decision-input fields.
The exporter still adds value only to a served ReadAck, and ReadReject and rejected ReadAck records still omit it.
StorageRead retains duplicated delivery under the shared max_dups = 1 budget, and RecvReadAck still delivers only awaited reads to the client.
Read actions still do not modify tok or myToks, and stale reads continue to use the same StaleTok definition as stale writes.
The shown P13–P17 edits preserve their named breaks and loci, and no P18 placement change appears in the diff.
answers still uses the attempt lookup and checks it against the storage decision, while emit still drops missing causes, preserving empty causes for mutation-only acks.
Votes and grant confirmations still use Conn, StepDown still uses q→n and Join n→q, while v3 eligibility, configurations and early timers are added around those directional rules.
The voter guard is now ~HearsLeader(q) \/ early[q], so a voter that still hears the leader may vote after a forward clock step.
CheckQuorum still steps down on loss of a connected majority, and adds leader ineligibility/removal, current-configuration eligible majorities and early clock timeouts.
Grant still records a heard request regardless of RepRoute and Resend remains, so the routing-fix replacement is retained without changing this entry's already-contradicted status again.
ReqRoute and RepRoute retain the lease-node relay, leaving X2.5 replaced by FR.1 as before; this diff does not change that status again.
ScheduleStep still selects one ng existentially, and StepLinks uses that same resolution for every occurrence within the step.
Cut/Drop and their exporter branches still emit the resolved listed pairs plus directed links, with heal records unchanged.
ReqRoute and RepRoute retain the one-hop lease-node relay, and FwdRoute applies the same one-hop pattern to forwarded reconfiguration requests.
Grant is still recorded without requiring RepRoute and Resend still retransmits without a new Grant, while v3 configuration epochs, counted agreements and decision inputs are added.
